id_and_class.summary: Aron Gurwitsch argues that conscious experience is always an organized field with three parts: a focal theme, a thematic field of unattended but relevant material, and a margin of co-present but irrelevant data. He fuses Gestalt principles of organization with Husserl's descriptive phenomenology and holds that this structure is an a priori feature of any field of consciousness. The field's own relations of relevance unify it, so no ego is needed to hold experience together.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Field of Theme, Context, and Margin

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is a dynamically organized whole, the field of consciousness, in which every content takes its character from its position relative to a theme.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Gurwitsch keeps Husserl's claim that consciousness is the source of all meaning but declines his transcendental idealism, adopting a levels-of-existence approach. Contemporary extensions look for neural and computational principles that could realize the field's organization.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed at the level of matter. Within experience, the field's unity arises from intrinsic relations among its contents, in the Gestalt sense that wholes have organization not derivable from parts.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Gurwitsch's conception is non-egological: no transcendental ego stands behind acts as their subject-pole. The psychic self of inner speech and the somatic self of posture are contents in the margin, which lets self-awareness pervade conscious life without a self standing over against it.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualities are never isolated atoms; each content has its character through its functional place in an organized whole.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Organized fields of experience; Gestalt wholes; relations of relevance among contents; the noema reinterpreted in Gestalt terms.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Eidetic phenomenological description of the field from the first-person standpoint, increasingly paired with experiments on attention and inattention.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three domains. The theme is what engrosses attention (a sentence, a melody, a face). The thematic field holds unattended material relevant to the theme (surrounding clauses, preceding notes). The margin holds co-present but irrelevant data in three standing categories: inner thoughts and speech, bodily posture, and the perceptual surroundings.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal structure; attention and inattention; marginal self-awareness; unity of consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Relevance: a structural relation among contents, distinct from intensity or attention, that decides whether a content belongs to the thematic field or the margin.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The field is continuously reorganized as relevance changes. A marginal sound that signals danger can become thematic, and the former theme recedes into the thematic field or margin.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The thematic field gives the theme its sense and organization, and the margin keeps body, world, and inner life continuously co-present.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity arises from the field's intrinsic organization and relations of relevance, not from a synthesizing act or a transcendental ego.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Contents are not processed one by one; each is experienced within a context. Yoshimi and Vinson link the field's holism to small-world network structure and its smooth and abrupt transitions to metastable dynamics and predictive coding.
core_claims_and_evidence: Every field of consciousness has the same three-part structure of theme, thematic field, and margin, as an a priori feature.
Relevance is a dimension of experience separate from attention, which extends William James's focus-and-fringe model.
The field needs no ego to unify it, since its organization supplies its unity.
Yoshimi and Vinson propose testing ‘causal relevance’ by varying peripheral contents while holding thematic contents fixed and checking whether later themes diverge.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological (eidetic description) drawing on Gestalt psychology, with empirical extensions in attention research.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Experiments on attention and inattentional contents; manipulations of peripheral contents to test causal relevance (Yoshimi and Vinson, 2015).
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The main dispute is whether the three-part structure is a priori, as Gurwitsch held, or a well-supported generalization about human experience. His non-egological view is a minority position against for-me-ness accounts of self-awareness.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Gurwitsch does not say how the field is physically realized. Yoshimi and Vinson raise open questions about the theme's size (it may expand, contract, or vanish) and how rich peripheral experience is.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The structural claim can be stated without any metaphysics of mind, which makes it compatible with several ontologies and a bridge to the cognitive science of attention.
